searchText: I think this should match with the NewPooledTransactionHashes eth/68 types. Legacy type is serialized as `0x00` if I am not wrong no it should be `0x80` `0x00` is invalid in RLP <@275441691312390144> that link you posted doesn't work for me, it doesn't seem to point to any specific place in the diff the encoding of receipts has changed in eth/69 to be the same across all tx types, so we are now including the type byte even for legacy transactions in the consensus encoding, receipts do not have a type byte at all Should point here yes it's correct like this for eth/68, we do not encode the type byte for legacy tx, so it's always > 0 (see condition in code). And the consensus encoding specifies tx-type to be exactly one byte. for eth/69, we encode it as an integer (0 = 0x80, 1 = 0x01, ...) This change from encoding as a byte to encoding as an integer - does it implicitly follow from some part of EIP? it just follows the eth/69 EIP: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7642#receipts-message-changes So `receipt = [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs]` means `tx-type` should be encoded now, instead of just written directly as a byte, is this correct? yes the previous encoding is weird, the eth/68 one I mean so for eth/68, we use the same encoding that is also used for hashing receipts in a block there, we encode legacy as just a list, and non-legacy as `rlp(type || [...])` this notation means: we create a byte slice containing `type` concatenated with the RLP list `[...]`, then we encode that byte array as RLP again in eth/69 it's much simpler, there is no 'nested' RLP byte array, and all the types are encoded the same notably, in eth/68, the `type` is not RLP-encoded at all, since it is just the prefix of the inner byte array yeah, it makes sense now, thanks could I get another status update about client readiness please? can I merge the spec update? should we do some more formalized testing, or should we just put eth/69 in client releases and work out any issues on the network? From Nethermind side - P2P communication with all messages changes works fine, but I still have a bit of work remaining on our peer strategies

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: the encoding of receipts has changed in eth/69 to be the same across all tx types, so we are now including the type byte even for legacy transactions

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: in the consensus encoding, receipts do not have a type byte at all

excerpts.author: alexb5dh
excerpts.content: Should point here

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: it's correct like this

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: for eth/68, we do not encode the type byte for legacy tx, so it's always > 0 (see condition in code). And the consensus encoding specifies tx-type to be exactly one byte.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: for eth/69, we encode it as an integer (0 = 0x80, 1 = 0x01, ...)

excerpts.author: alexb5dh
excerpts.content: This change from encoding as a byte to encoding as an integer - does it implicitly follow from some part of EIP?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: it just follows the eth/69 EIP: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7642#receipts-message-changes

excerpts.author: alexb5dh
excerpts.content: So `receipt = [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs]` means `tx-type` should be encoded now, instead of just written directly as a byte, is this correct?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: the previous encoding is weird, the eth/68 one I mean

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: so for eth/68, we use the same encoding that is also used for hashing receipts in a block

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: there, we encode legacy as just a list, and non-legacy as `rlp(type || [...])`

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: this notation means: we create a byte slice containing `type` concatenated with the RLP list `[...]`, then we encode that byte array as RLP again

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: in eth/69 it's much simpler, there is no 'nested' RLP byte array, and all the types are encoded the same

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: notably, in eth/68, the `type` is not RLP-encoded at all, since it is just the prefix of the inner byte array
